title: Definition 4.1: Absolute (Global) Extrema
Definition 4.2: Local (Relative) Extrema
content:
\textbf{Local Maximum:} $f(c)$ is a \textbf{local maximum} if there exists an open interval $(a, b)$ containing $c$ such that:
\[
f(c) \geq f(x) \quad \text{for all } x \in (a, b)
\]

\textbf{Local Minimum:} $f(c)$ is a \textbf{local minimum} if there exists an open interval $(a, b)$ containing $c$ such that:
\[
f(c) \leq f(x) \quad \text{for all } x \in (a, b)
\]

\textcolor{primaryblue}{\faInfoCircle\ \textbf{Key Differences:}}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{|p{5.5cm}|p{6.5cm}|}
\hline
\rowcolor{primaryblue!20}
\textbf{Local Extrema} & \textbf{Absolute Extrema} \\
\hline
Highest/lowest in a neighbourhood & Highest/lowest on entire domain \\
\hline
Can have many local max/min & At most one absolute max/min \\
\hline
Every absolute extremum is local & Not every local extremum is absolute \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

content:
\textcolor{primaryblue}{\textbf{Problem:}} Show that the equation $x^3 + x - 1 = 0$ has exactly one real root.

\vspace{0.3cm}
\textcolor{primaryblue}{\textbf{Solution:}}

Let $f(x) = x^3 + x - 1$.

\textbf{Step 1:} Show that a root exists (using Intermediate Value Theorem)

\begin{align*}
f(0) &= -1 < 0 \\
f(1) &= 1 + 1 - 1 = 1 > 0
\end{align*}

Since $f$ is continuous and changes sign, by IVT there exists at least one $r \in (0, 1)$ with $f(r) = 0$. \textcolor{green}{\checkmark}

\textbf{Step 2:} Show the root is unique (using Rolle's Theorem by contradiction)

Suppose there are two distinct roots $r_1$ and $r_2$ with $r_1 < r_2$.

Then $f(r_1) = 0$ and $f(r_2) = 0$, so $f(r_1) = f(r_2)$.

Since $f$ is a polynomial, it is continuous on $[r_1, r_2]$ and differentiable on $(r_1, r_2)$.

By Rolle's Theorem, there exists $c \in (r_1, r_2)$ such that $f'(c) = 0$.

But:
\[
f'(x) = 3x^2 + 1 \geq 1 > 0 \quad \text{for all } x
\]

So $f'(x)$ is never zero! This is a contradiction.

\textbf{Conclusion:} The assumption of two distinct roots must be false. Therefore, the equation has \textbf{exactly one real root}.

\textbf{Answer:} \boxed{\text{Exactly one real root exists}}

\textcolor{primaryblue}{\faLightbulb\ \textbf{Key Technique:}} Rolle's Theorem can be used to prove uniqueness of roots by contradiction!

Theorem 4.5: Increasing/Decreasing Test (First Derivative Test for Monotonicity)
content:
Let $f$ be continuous on $[a, b]$ and differentiable on $(a, b)$.

\textbf{(a)} If $f'(x) > 0$ for all $x \in (a, b)$, then $f$ is \textbf{increasing} on $[a, b]$.

\textbf{(b)} If $f'(x) < 0$ for all $x \in (a, b)$, then $f$ is \textbf{decreasing} on $[a, b]$.

\textbf{(c)} If $f'(x) = 0$ for all $x \in (a, b)$, then $f$ is \textbf{constant} on $[a, b]$.

\textcolor{primaryblue}{\faInfoCircle\ \textbf{Proof Idea:}}

This follows directly from the Mean Value Theorem! If $x_1 < x_2$ in $(a,b)$, then:
\[
f(x_2) - f(x_1) = f'(c)(x_2 - x_1)
\]

for some $c \in (x_1, x_2)$.

If $f'(c) > 0$ and $x_2 - x_1 > 0$, then $f(x_2) - f(x_1) > 0$, so $f(x_2) > f(x_1)$ (increasing).

\textcolor{accentorange}{\faExclamationTriangle\ \textbf{Important Subtlety:}}

$f'(x) \geq 0$ (allowing $f' = 0$ at isolated points) still implies $f$ is increasing. For example, $f(x) = x^3$ has $f'(0) = 0$, but $f$ is still increasing on $\mathbb{R}$.

\vspace{0.5cm}

title: Definition 4.8: Sign Chart Method
content:
To find intervals of increase/decrease:

\textbf{Step 1:} Find all critical numbers (where $f'(x) = 0$ or $f'$ undefined)

\textbf{Step 2:} Plot critical numbers on a number line to divide it into intervals

\textbf{Step 3:} Choose a test point in each interval and evaluate $f'(\text{test point})$

\textbf{Step 4:} Create a sign chart:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
\rowcolor{primaryblue!20}
\textbf{Interval} & \textbf{Sign of $f'$} & \textbf{Behavior of $f$} \\
\hline
$(a, c_1)$ & $+$ or $-$ & Increasing or Decreasing \\
\hline
$(c_1, c_2)$ & $+$ or $-$ & Increasing or Decreasing \\
\hline
$\vdots$ & $\vdots$ & $\vdots$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\textbf{Step 5:} State intervals of increase and decrease

title: Problem 30: Optimization -- Applications
content:
(a) A company produces $x$ units at cost $C(x) = 500 + 20x + 0.1x^2$ dollars. The revenue from selling $x$ units is $R(x) = 100x - 0.2x^2$ dollars. Find the production level that maximizes profit.

(b) A printed page is to have total area 80 cm² with 1 cm margins on top and bottom and 2 cm margins on each side. What dimensions maximize the printed area?

(c) Find the point on the line $y = 2x + 1$ that is closest to the origin.

(d) A Norman window has the shape of a rectangle surmounted by a semicircle. If the perimeter is fixed at 30 feet, find the dimensions that admit the most light.

(e) A closed cylindrical can is to be made with $300\pi$ cm² of material (including top and bottom). Find the dimensions that maximize the volume.

(f) A track is to be built in the shape of a rectangle with semicircles at each end. The inside of the track must enclose an area of 10,000 m². Find the dimensions that minimize the perimeter.
